subject: POC trial environment decision: hosted vs VPC vs dedicated sandbox
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: POC trial environment decision: hosted vs VPC vs dedicated sandbox

Hi Alice / Bob —

Thanks again for the call today — great discussion about the three use cases you want to validate in the POC. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture the proposed success criteria, a short evaluation plan, and the environment options (hosted trial, dedicated sandbox, or VPC trial) so your team can pick the right path.

Proposed success criteria (high level):
- Latency under 250ms 95th pct for our critical inference route (prompt size ~512 tokens)
- Token cost within 30% of your benchmark (current vendor baseline)
- No impact to PII — all data either redacted or stays in your VPC for the VPC option
- Integration: embeddings/semantic search + chat pipeline validated end-to-end

Evaluation plan (2–4 weeks, adjustable):
1) Week 0: environment setup and smoke tests (connectivity, API keys, simple queries)
2) Week 1: run representative workload (batch + streaming), capture perf/cost
3) Week 2: quality evaluation on your test set + regression checks
4) Week 3: finalize findings and recommended next steps

Environment options (tradeoffs):
- Hosted trial (fastest): Redwood-hosted, scoped trial project. Minimal setup, start within 24–48h. Best for quick performance/cost signal but not suitable if you need data to stay in your network.
- Dedicated sandbox (reserved capacity): Isolated GPUs in our Dedicated offering. More predictable throughput; provisioning ~1–2 weeks depending on sizing. Good for high-throughput tests without VPC complexity.
- VPC trial (preferred for security): We deploy into your VPC or a customer-managed subnet in your cloud. Requires security review (KMS, IP allowlist, peering) and typically 2–4 weeks to get to smoke-test.

Recommended next steps:
- Please confirm which environment you prefer. If VPC, we’ll need: preferred cloud region, IP ranges, KMS key ARN (or let us use customer-managed key our side), and an SRE contact.
- I’ve attached a short technical requirements doc that outlines the items we’ll ask for to spin up a VPC trial.
- We’ll draft a short SOW for the trial and share timelines once the environment is confirmed.

Attachments: POC_Technical_Requirements.pdf
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/u/0/folders/POC-AcmeAI

Thanks — I’ll loop Dev for the technical follow-up once you confirm.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Can you loop in your security lead? I’ll also bring our procurement contact if we need to run a short SOW.

Hi team — quick technical notes from an SRE perspective.

Summary of what we’ll implement for the VPC trial (high level):
- Network: create a private endpoint in your VPC and set up VPC peering (or use PrivateLink). We’ll provide a CIDR suggestion for the peering range; allowlist our NAT egress IPs for callback/webhook traffic.
- Auth: use short-lived API tokens and optional mTLS for internal services. For SSO, we can integrate with OIDC/SAML if you want user-level access.
- KMS: we support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS & GCP CMEK). We’ll need decrypt/encrypt grant to the service principal.
- Logs/metrics: push metrics to your Prometheus / CloudWatch. Request/response logs (if required) can be written to an S3/GCS bucket in your account.
- KV cache & model files: model weights will be cached on Redwood nodes; no model weights are written into your bucket.

Suggested minimal onboarding checklist (what we need to start):
1) Cloud region & preferred availability zone
2) IP allowlist / CIDR for peering
3) KMS key ARN + principal to grant permissions
4) Service account email (for role grants) or IAM role to assume
5) Contact: primary SRE + secondary ops contact

Estimated engineering time: ~3–5 business days to configure peering & keys + 2 business days for smoke tests. If your security team needs additional artifacts (network diagrams / threat model), we can generate those in parallel.

I’ll attach a short sample network policy snippet and a minimal Terraform example in the shared Drive.

Thanks — Dev
